sources.citation: Snethlage, Emil Heinrich. 1935 [publ. 1936]. Nachrichten über die Pauserna-Guarayú, die Siriono am Rio Baures und die S. Simonianes in der Nähe der Serra S. Simon. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 67(5/6): 278-293 (S. Simonianes: pp. 292-293, vocabulary p. 293).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the article (checked scanned text for Betonung/Akzent/Ton/Aussprache and read pp. 292-293 in full plus the page image). The only pronunciation remarks are the open-vowel hook and 'consonants as in German'. However the page image shows that Snethlage wrote an acute accent on almost every S. Simonianes form (natá, wokén, oą́n, njąín, utín, olehín, hokepéin, kabeßín, mänihi [accent on i], topán, päréín, pipín, pökín, sóu, páąn, päú, päí, apá, tabá), i.e. accent MARKS on a 19-item wordlist without any statement of what they denote: wordlist-only…

sources.note: Modern specialist treatment that re-examines Snethlage's Sansimoniano list against Chiquitano varieties (per Nikulin 2020:29, includes a phonological analysis of the poorly attested Chiquitano-family varieties); the only modern work likely to comment on the transcription, including any accent marks.
